title: Strict-system projection formula composition coherence
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$ and its algebraic closure $k$
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer
$\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put
$A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated
finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ be separated
finite-type $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
For $W=X,Y,Z$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and $R_W=\lim_n B_{n,W}$
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the
abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $B_{n,W}$-module sheaves:
its objects have $B_{n+1,W}$-linear transitions
$M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1,W}\to B_{n,W}}M_n$, and its
morphisms are componentwise module maps commuting with transitions
[lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In $D(\mathscr S_W)$ let
$\mathscr N_W$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems, meaning
that every transition-adjoint map
$M_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,W}}B_{n,W}\to M_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\ge n$,
whose levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$, the bounded constructible
finite-Tor category [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower,
def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

Use the simultaneous geometric section models of pullback, derived tensor,
open extension, proper direct image and their adjunction maps from
[lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For $h=f,g,gf$, let
$\mathcal F_h$ be the specified strict-system compact-support realization
of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization], and let
$\alpha_{g,f}:\mathcal F_g\mathcal F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_{gf}$
be the geometric compact-support composition comparison of
[thm-sf-comp-composition], formed in these same simultaneous models.
For $h:U\to V$, $P\in\mathscr N_U$, $Q\in\mathscr N_V$, write
$$
\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}_{h,P,Q}:
\mathcal F_hP\otimes^L Q\longrightarrow
\mathcal F_h(P\otimes^L h^*Q)
$$
for the strict-system realization of the specified projection transformation
[def-exchange-projection]: the proper direct-image counit-defined projection
mate followed by the open-extension tensor comparison in a compactification.
All these maps use the quotient transitions of the same models; they are
not independently chosen lifts of their finite evaluations.

These projection maps are natural in $P,Q$ and satisfy, for
$M\in\mathscr N_X$ and $N\in\mathscr N_Z$, the identity
$$
\alpha_{g,f,M\otimes^L f^*g^*N}\,
\mathcal F_g\!\left(\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}_{f,M,g^*N}\right)\,
\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}_{g,\mathcal F_fM,N}
=
\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}_{gf,M,N}\,
(\alpha_{g,f,M}\otimes1_N).
$$
Both sides have source $\mathcal F_g\mathcal F_fM\otimes^L N$ and target
$\mathcal F_{gf}(M\otimes^L(gf)^*N)$, using the canonical pullback,
tensor and associator identifications. This is an equality in
$D(\mathscr S_Z)$ before total derived inverse limit. Its level-$n$
evaluations are the specified finite projection identities. The functor
$\mathcal L_Z=R\lim\circ U_Z$ of
[lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with $U_Z$ termwise
restriction to $R_Z$-module towers, carries this equality to the equality
of its total-limit images.

source.place: Proof, sentences 'The composition, refinement, exchange and proper-coincidence identities are [prop-sf-pf-coherence]' and 'Every step constructs or compares the same projection map'. The strict-system equality stated here is an additional agent-formulated obligation, made explicit in the existing DAG proof of fix-prop-projection-formula, Step 11; the blueprint paragraph itself does not state it.

proof.text: Work on the diagram site $\mathcal D_W=J^{\mathrm{op}}\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, with coverings in the site direction as in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. On it use the varying ring sheaf $\mathcal B_W(n,U)=B_{n,W}(U)$ with its quotient maps. The sheaf condition is checked for each $n$; giving a module action on a sheaf on $\mathcal D_W$ is exactly giving the component $B_{n,W}$-actions and semilinear transitions, because the action's naturality in $J$ is precisely that semilinearity equation. This identifies $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal B_W)$ exactly and additively with $\mathscr S_W$, not with towers tensored over the constant ring $\mathcal O_E$. Apply the simultaneous-model clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]: inverse image, derived direct image, tensor, open extension, and the specified units, counits and mates are realized together on these ringed diagram sites. These are the same constructions used to define $\mathcal F_h$ in [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization] and $\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}$ in the statement. For a geometric map $u$ write $P_u=u^*$ and $R_u=Ru_*$ on the diagram sites. By [def-exchange-projection] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], its direct-image projection map $\pi_{u;H,Q}$ is the $P_u\dashv R_u$ transpose of $(\varepsilon_{u,H}\otimes1)\mu_u$, where $\mu_u$ is the tensor-pullback comparison. This construction is natural in both inputs; composing it with the natural open tensor map proves the required naturality of $\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}$.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); agent application on the ringed diagram site to the specified simultaneous constructions

proof.text:
First calculate for two direct images on these diagram sites. Under the canonical derived compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], prove
$$\pi_{vu;H,Q}=R_v(\pi_{u;H,P_vQ})\,\pi_{v;R_uH,Q}.$$
Transpose both sides under $P_uP_v\dashv R_vR_u$. The composite counit is $\varepsilon_u\circ P_u\varepsilon_vR_u$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Expanding the defining transposes, both become
$$P_uP_v(R_vR_uH\otimes Q)\longrightarrow P_uP_vR_vR_uH\otimes P_uP_vQ\xrightarrow{P_u\varepsilon_{v,R_uH}\otimes1}P_uR_uH\otimes P_uP_vQ\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{u,H}\otimes1}H\otimes P_uP_vQ.$$
Here naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] moves the intermediate counit through the tensor comparison. The iterated tensor comparisons coincide on flat-term K-flat representatives supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]: both send each local pure tensor to that same pure tensor, with the identical total-complex signs. Thus these are equal transposes, and the adjunction bijection gives the displayed equality in the derived category of systems itself. This argument does not require a Tor bound or invertibility of $\pi_u$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); agent transpose calculation, as in the existing DAG proof of fix-prop-projection-formula, Step 7

proof.text:
Next let $k:A\hookrightarrow B$, $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be quasi-compact opens, $r:A\to C$, $p:B\to D$ proper, and $pk=ir$. Use the geometric normalization of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]: put $B_C=B\times_D C$, let $s:A\hookrightarrow B_C$ be its clopen component, and form $a:P_pi_!\to k_!P_r$ by open base change followed by the projection which is identity on $s(A)$ and zero on the complement. On the varying-ring diagram sites these maps exist by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and exact open extension [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; all are $\mathcal B$-linear since restriction and component projection preserve the scalar action. Define their proper-adjunction mate
$$\gamma=R_p(k_!\varepsilon_r)\,R_p(aR_r)\,\eta_pi_!R_r:i_!R_r\longrightarrow R_pk_!.$$
This uses the formula and geometric clopen description of the cited tower lemma, not an application of its constant-ring tensor product to varying-ring modules. Write $\delta_j:j_!H\otimes Q\to j_!(H\otimes P_jQ)$ for the open tensor comparison obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] and K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The proper/open tensor-mate identity is the statement of [lem-pur-system-clopen-tensor-compatibility], applied to this square; its formula uses exactly the same $a$, $\gamma$, $\pi$ and $\delta$. Thus the required identity holds in the derived system category before evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), open case; agent tensor/mate calculation on the varying-ring diagram site, using sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text: For the bounded constructible inputs used below, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies the finite etale-origin witnesses. At each $n$ apply [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] to a constant tower with $B=A_n$: the evaluated proper/open map is an isomorphism. Preservation of the specified mate construction by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identifies this with the evaluation of $\gamma$ on varying-ring systems. Evaluations detect isomorphisms by that same section theorem, so $\gamma$ is an isomorphism on these inputs. This uses isomorphism detection only, and requires no common lower bound in $n$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), open case; agent tensor/mate calculation on the varying-ring diagram site, using sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text:
Choose compatible compactifications. The schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the field $k$, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Choose $g=si$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] to obtain $f=qj$ and $gf=(sp)(bj)$, with $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open, $s:\overline Y\to Z$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, $q:V\to Y$ proper, and $pb=iq$ Cartesian. Proper compactifications are again finite type over $k$, so all opens involved are quasi-compact. In the fixed simultaneous models the geometric composition comparison is
$$R_si_!R_qj_!\xrightarrow{R_s\gamma j_!}R_sR_pb_!j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{sp}(bj)_!.$$
The last arrow uses the derived direct-image compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and open composition [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], realized together by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The proper/open map has exactly the mate normalization in Step 3; its finite normalization is specified by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] and [thm-sf-comp-composition]. This is the geometric $\alpha_{g,f}$ assumed in the statement, constructed in the same section models; it is not identified with that map merely by matching finite evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), first paragraph and displayed compactification diagram; strict-system realization is the agent application of the specified models

proof.text:
Expand $\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}$ through these compactifications using [def-exchange-projection]. Put $T=M\otimes P_fP_gN$. The left side of the asserted identity first applies the following four maps, then $\alpha_{g,f,T}$:
$$R_si_!R_qj_!M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\pi_s}R_s(i_!R_qj_!M\otimes P_sN)\xrightarrow{R_s\delta_i}R_si_!(R_qj_!M\otimes P_iP_sN)\xrightarrow{R_si_!\pi_q}R_si_!R_q(j_!M\otimes P_qP_iP_sN)\xrightarrow{R_si_!R_q\delta_j}R_si_!R_qj_!T.$$
Insert the formula for $\alpha$ from Step 5. Move its proper/open factor $R_s\gamma$ to the left of $R_s\delta_i$ and $R_si_!\pi_q$ by the equality of Step 3 with $(r,p,k,i)=(q,p,b,i)$ and $Q=P_sN$; its movement past $\delta_j$ is the naturality of $\gamma$ in its input. Move it past $\pi_s$ by naturality of $\pi_s$. The two proper projection maps now combine to $\pi_{sp}$ by Step 2. The remaining two open tensor maps combine to $\delta_{bj}$: under the canonical open composition of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], both are the identity on a local tensor supported on $X$ and zero off $X$, using the extension/tensor map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. Their derived versions follow on the same K-flat models [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The resulting composite is precisely $\operatorname{PF}^{\mathrm{sys}}_{gf,M,N}(\alpha_{g,f,M}\otimes1_N)$, with pullback identifications $P_jP_qP_iP_s=P_{gf}$. Thus the required equality holds in $D(\mathscr S_Z)$ for these compactifications.

proof.text: For other chosen compactifications, use the actual refinement comparison $\theta_u=R_{p_2}(\gamma_u^{-1})c_{p_2,u}$, formed in the same models. The strict-system refinement identity [lem-pur-system-compactification-pf-substitution] gives $\theta_{u,T}\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}(\theta_{u,M}\otimes1)$ and supplies the system cocycle for these comparisons. The common geometric refinements of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] therefore conjugate the equality of Step 6 to the equality for the specified models of $f,g,gf$. The simultaneous constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] carry these actual comparisons to the finite comparisons of [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism]. Equality of arbitrary system morphisms is never inferred from equality of evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), compactification composite and independence-of-choices argument; explicit projection substitution is agent-written

proof.text: Check domains and finite evaluations. Open extensions of the finite-Tor constructible levels remain finite-Tor constructible, with the same cohomological range, by [lem-trf-open-ctf]. Thus the proper/open comparisons used on $j_!M$ and in refinements have bounded constructible levels. The realization [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization] carries $M$ to $\mathcal F_fM\in\mathscr N_Y$. Pullback preserves each bounded constructible finite-Tor level by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], and tensor preserves it by [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii), adding the two finite Tor intervals separately at each $n$. Apply [lem-pur-system-normalized-tensor-closure] to the quotient-ring systems and the morphisms of their pro-etale topoi. It identifies the actual transition-adjoint maps for pullback and tensor with the invertible reduction comparisons. Thus these systems are normalized without flat coefficient transitions or a uniform bound in $n$. Hence every occurrence of $\mathcal F_h$ in the desired identity has the domain required in the statement. At each $n\ge1$, evaluation preserves the actual units, counits, tensor comparisons and mates by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Therefore it takes the system equality of Steps 6–7 to the composition identity for the specified finite maps of [def-exchange-projection] and the finite compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. The constructible levels have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so the proper/open and compactification comparisons have their stated witnessed domains. The finite maps in particular agree with the pro-etale realization in [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. This checks which finite identity has been obtained; it is not used to infer the system equality.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); finite evaluations of the preceding agent calculation

proof.text: Finally apply the functor $\mathcal L_Z=R\lim\circ U_Z$ to the equality in $D(\mathscr S_Z)$. The evaluation calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] defines $U_Z$ termwise and $\mathcal L_Z$ as a derived functor. Functoriality sends the established equality of the two composites to equality of their total-limit images, as asserted.

Realizes the main-20261015 fix-prop-projection-formula sentences about composition/refinement identities and the same specified projection map; the strict-system details are additional agent arguments following Stacks 0F7B, 0F7J, 0B56, 0E8I and 07A4.

tool_uses.why: The unit, counit, mate, and simultaneous quotient-transition section models are used throughout; this is the unit tool supplying the strict-system realization.
The finite-level compact-support realization and its domain statement are used in the domain check.
The final termwise restriction and total-limit functor are used to transport the established system equality.
Etale-origin witnesses are required for the finite proper/open comparison domains.
Open extension preserves bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude in the domain check.
Tensor preserves finite-Tor constructibility with summed Tor intervals.
The final finite evaluations are identified with the specified pro-etale compact-support projection maps.

Step 7: conjugation by theta and the cocycle. Step 8: domains. Step 9: elementary. New nodes: (1) the clopen tensor-mate identity is true. Both P_{p1}-transposes reduce to the tensor compatibility of a, since open base change is monoidal and the clopen projection is multiplicative. Tested on an empty component, identity verticals and a Cartesian square. (2) The refinement intertwining is true, from (1) and pi composition. The cocycle holds by vertical pasting, and independence of the common refinement by the closure argument. Its normalized-ctf hypotheses are exactly what step 7 supplies. (3) Normalized tensor and pullback closure is true for arbitrary rings, because derived base change is monoidal. Tested with Z/l^n on a point. It partly overlaps lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison for pullback only, so it is not a duplicate.
